samples.title: That Far-Away Look
samples.relation: Lahr argues that Holmes's crime-solving is an art rather than a forensic science: like his inspiration Oscar Wilde, Holmes is an aesthete whose 'aesthetic sight' perceives the criminal-artist's design in clues, so that Watson the philistine ('What ineffable twaddle!') consistently misses what is self-evident to Holmes. He suggests Plato would say Holmes sees only the perfect Forms behind appearances, and reads the BBC adaptations accordingly: in The Case of the Silk Stocking Holmes's trance-like perception of the victims' pedicured feet reveals a killer with a foot fetish, while Sherlock's 'A Study in Pink' renders his insight as first-person vision with on-screen data. samples.book: 096 - Hannibal Lecter and Philosophy - The Heart of the Matter
samples.title: 13. An Aesthete par Excellence
samples.relation: Holt argues that the key to Lecter is aestheticism: the Goldberg Variations scoring his nightstick killing of the Memphis guard is no camouflage, because art, cannibalism, murder and etiquette are all unified by aesthetic value prized apart from the good and the true. His 'ACME question' applies inference to the best explanation to show that a single hypothesis — the aesthetic — explains Art, Cannibalism, Murder and Etiquette together, with 'Discourtesy is unspeakably ugly to me' read as an aesthetic rather than a moral complaint. samples.relation: Joe Slater builds a two-premise anti-natalist argument from Shelley's Paradise Lost epigraph ('Did I request thee, Maker, from my clay / To mould me man?'): since it is wrong to inflict harm on an autonomous being without consent, and every autonomous life inevitably contains harms, creating autonomous beings - Adam in the lab or a baby in the womb - is wrong. He answers the objection from Parfit's non-identity problem via the damaged-brain Adam case, and defends the Harm Premise with Mill's On Liberty: consent matters because autonomous agents must be free to harm themselves, as with the smoker, the drinker, and Frankenstein's stolen kidney. samples.relation: Cogburn and Hebert ask how fantasy can stage magic that is by definition indescribable, from Lovecraft's unknowable mirror-monster in 'The Outsider' to Priest's limit-of-thought paradoxes. They sort magic into formulaic natural magic — mage-scientists exploiting a world's universal laws, exactly Kant's conception of nature, as in Snape's potions or Mieville's steampunk — and sublimate natural magic, where the practitioner surrenders to forces as in Candomblé possession or Robin Hobb's possessed soldier, against genuinely unnatural magic that violates law itself, as in Bakker's Prince of Nothing or the reality-liquefying passage from Sartre's Nausea. Carroll's theory of art-horror (via Mary Douglas: impurity as categorical incompatibility and incompleteness, from Leviticus's shellfish to The Dunwich Horror's fusions, fissions, and formlessness) explains how writers express the inexpressible, and exposes why 4e's algorithmic spell rules — the Fireball math every player masters 'like a chemistry student' — naturalize magic and kill the horror, leaving Dungeon Masters only narrative techniques (character reaction, reader-relative impossibility, limit impossibility) rather than rules.

samples.relation: Cogburn and Hebert sort fantasy magic into formulaic natural magic (wizards as scientists exploiting a world's universal laws, in Kant's sense of nature—Salvatore's Cadderly, Snape's potions, Eberron's Artificer), sublimate natural magic (shamans, sorcerers, and warlocks surrendering to forces, as in African diaspora possession religions), and unnatural magic that violates a world's laws, whose horror Sartre's Nausea passage about flesh rebelling captures. samples.title: Only Time Will Tell

samples.title: The Philosophy of Popular Culture
samples.relation: King analyzes The Limey as 'Get Carter as made by Alain Resnais,' using Bordwell's fabula/syuzhet distinction to show how its nonlinear editing renders what Soderbergh calls the nonlinear nature of thought. samples.title: Summarizing the Future
samples.relation: Applying Bergson's Time and Free Will claim that recalling the past shortens it into a 'thing', the section uses the curriculum-vitae metaphor: like a CV or Facebook page, we imagine the future as a summary compiled from the past. In 'Paycheck', Jennings's sack becomes a plan only when he reflects - the wire at the police station, the token on the bus - until past, present and future fuse and he feels 'a strange elation' at fulfilling his past self's design, raising again whether awareness of the future changes what we do. The film diverges by having Jennings sabotage the atomic-bomb future he foresees, echoing Minority Report's contest between an inevitable future and present action.

samples.title: Cobol’s Backyard
samples.relation: Malloy argues the real players of Inception are the corporations — Cobol Engineering hires Cobb to spy on Saito, Saito as CEO of Proclus Global buys the airline and commissions the Fischer job, and the human characters are pawns moved at the firms' will. He builds a case that corporations are moral persons because they make decisions through their own procedures, hold rights (Saito's 'I bought the airline' exercised Proclus's property rights through a representative), and bear responsibilities not reducible to CEOs or shareholders, rebuffing Harman-style objections from moral emotions and virtues by comparing corporations to psychopaths, who are persons without being good ones. He ends with Fischer-Morrow's impending energy monopoly: Friedman's shareholder-primacy view versus the corporation's duty to the moral community, and what corporate personhood means for real-world practices like boycotts.

samples.title: Too Big to Function
samples.relation: Terjesen argues Jack's combined title, Vice President of East Coast Television and Microwave Oven Programming, exhibits the corporate mentality: following Robert Jackall's Moral Mazes, credit flows up (Jack's Trivection oven) and blame flows down (Greenzo, the fireworks fiasco), so managers learn to avoid decisive action. Peter French's thesis that corporations are moral persons explains why GE runs fine with Don Geiss in a coma and Kathy Geiss playing with unicorns, so no one at the top needs to understand the businesses they oversee. MacIntyre's distinction between practices with internal goods and external rewards shows profit-thinking erasing comedy's internal good, turning TGS into 'pos-mens' and product integration, and Adam Smith's attack on distant, ignorant regulators is turned against conglomerate central management itself.

The chapter frames Lynch and Frost as Romantics — Novalis on wonder, Isaiah Berlin's Roots of Romanticism on the artist's inner vision — who break three storytelling rules (authors create stories, protagonists solve problems, stories have endings), so that Laura's mystery stays a living Jack-the-Ripper-style mystery and the story becomes a meta-narrative co-created with viewers, echoing Buddhist pratityasamutpada and Russell's beginningless world. samples.relation: In a Platonic dialogue, Ronald Green and D.E. samples.title: Rāma of Gilead
samples.relation: Matthew Butkus reads Roland Deschain of The Dark Tower as a parallel to Rama of the Ramayana and Arjuna of the Bhagavad Gita, mapping his cyclical existence onto the Hindu concepts of karma (his coupling with the demon spawning Mordred, letting Jake fall), dharma (the gunslinger's duty to protect the Beams as an avatar restoring cosmic order), samskara (character shaped by all past lives) and samsara (the death-rebirth cycle the Horn of Eld may or may not break). Like Krishna instructing the reluctant Arjuna, the text tells Roland he must 'stand and be true' regardless of misgivings; Butkus concludes the moral for readers is not violence but fulfilling one's own svadharma—to stand and be true in one's own station.

samples.book: 165 - The Good Place and Philosophy - Everything Is Forking Fine!
samples.title: 19. Hinduism Gets More than Five Percent Right
samples.relation: Argues Hinduism 'gets more than five percent right' via the Bhagavad Gita: the show's point system mirrors karma, Eleanor's failed point-chasing and quiet departure for the Bad Place enact nishkama karma (desire-less action), and the 802 reboots are rebirths without memory. The characters form a ladder of unfoldment — Jason's unknowing wrong action below Eleanor's knowing one, Tahani's corruptly motivated good deeds, Chidi's knowledge without decision, Michael swerving from his demonic dharma, and Janet highest: desireless, rebooting like cyclical rebirth, her void echoing boundless Brahman. Chidi's logic-bound indecision versus Eleanor's knowledge-producing logic completes the Gita reading.

samples.book: 105 - The Ultimate Game of Thrones and Philosophy - You Think or Die
samples.title: 22. The Many-Faced God and Indian Philosophy
samples.relation: Van Eyghen maps the Faceless Men onto Indian philosophy: their one God of many faces parallels Vedanta's Brahman in personal form as Ishvara, and Arya's training to become 'no one' parallels shedding the ego toward identity with Brahman - with Jaqen as guru and the stick-beating ritual as an example of identity fusion in Harvey Whitehouse's cognitive science of religion. But the Faceless Men may go further than Vedanta toward Buddhism, since they worship a god with no face of his own and aim at no-self rather than union, while Arya's pragmatic adoption of the shellfish-merchant disguise echoes the Bhagavad Gita's Krishna: perform your duty without attachment to any self.

samples.book: 275 - Hunting – Philosophy for Everyone - In Search of the Wild Life
samples.title: Hunting Philosophy for Everyone
samples.relation: Wawatie and Pyne present a traditional Algonquin Anishinabe philosophy of hunting in which all creation — humans, animals, plants, water, rocks — belongs to one family bound by spirit, and hunting is a reciprocal relationship of gift, gratitude, and non-waste rather than a contest. Through Kokom Lena Nottaway's creation story (animals gifting a foggy figure wisdom, vision, strength until humans take form) and the life of 'Nathan' learning the moose, they show hunting as 'a quest for understanding.' A hunting song teaches by indirect clues, letting the learner reach their own awareness, and feast ceremonies honor the prey's sacrifice.

samples.book: 160 - Fallout and Philosophy - Thinking Outside the Shelter
samples.title: Notes
samples.relation: The Funkes apply Clark and Chalmers's extended mind hypothesis to the Pip-Boy, arguing it meets all three criteria for cognitive extension - availability (worn at all times), reliability (trusted rad and health monitoring), and active cognitive engagement (V.A.T.S. offloads targeting calculations) - so it is part of the Sole Survivor's and Courier's minds, as in 'The Glowing Sea' and the search for Virgil's cure. Donna Haraway's cyborg frames this human-machine hybridity alongside cyberdogs and Kellogg, but Fallout inverts her liberationist vision: the Pip-Boy is a survival lifeline forced by the wasteland, not an emancipatory choice, making the cyborg a dystopian necessity. Comparing the Pip-Boy with cochlear implants, prosthetics, and brain-computer interfaces, and the Old World Blues Think Tank with a dehumanizing bio-tech extreme, the chapter uses Alison Kafer's feminist crip critique to insist real augmentation carries pain, stigma, and unequal access the game's frictionless fiction erases, closing on a cautious transhumanist note.

samples.book: 141 - Avatar_ The Last Airbender and Philosophy - Wisdom from Aang to Zuko
samples.title: The Proud Disabled Person as Counterstory
samples.relation: Argues that Toph Beifong is not the harmful 'Supercrip' stereotype (an exceptional individual who overcomes disability through talent and grit, which blames ordinary disabled people for their disadvantage) but a 'Proud Disabled Person' counterstory. Her blindness is a disability gain: it led her to learn earthbending from the badgermoles, the original earthbenders, and to live immersed in bending as her constant way of navigating the world, deepening her mastery. Using Hilde Lindemann's master narratives and counterstories and Elizabeth Barnes's mere-difference view, the chapter shows Toph fits neither the 'better off dead' nor the 'irrationally happy' stereotype: she is grumpy, nuanced (adapting her teaching of Aang in 'Bitter Work'), and a central driver of the plot rather than a moral prop. Fricker's hermeneutical injustice explains why disabled viewers struggle to make sense of flourishing with a disability, and why Toph's portrait gives them permission to celebrate it.

samples.book: 063 - Philip K. Dick and Philosophy - Do Androids Have Kindred Spirits
samples.title: Chapter 30 - “The Golden Man”
samples.relation: Jeremy Pierce reads 'The Golden Man' through the Aristotle-Lucretius dispute over purposes in nature: Cris Johnson, the precognitive golden mutant, first terrifies the DCA as Homo superior, 'a deeve who would be to us what we are to the great apes', until George Baines finds 'virtually no frontal lobe... It's nothing but an animal' choosing by reflex rather than reflection. Aristotle's teleology - normal development suiting what is objectively good for a human being - makes sense of calling one-armed growth, autism's deficits, or Cris's missing inner life deficiencies, while Lucretius's anti-teleology, largely adopted by the autism community, permits talk only of the typical and atypical. The chapter argues the characters' horror at humanity's replacement by reflex-driven breeders is unintelligible unless something is genuinely missing that is natural and healthy for human offspring.

samples.book: 145 - The Big Bang Theory and Philosophy - Rock, Paper, Scissors, Aristotle, Locke
samples.title: The Big Bang Theory and Philosophy
samples.relation: Clifton asks whether fans are moral monsters for laughing at behavior that looks autistic, running Sheldon through the DSM criteria for Asperger's syndrome: missing Penny's sarcasm about doctors who 'remove shoes from asses,' hedging the bath-item Christmas gift, and inflexibly clinging to nonfunctional routines like Saturday-night laundry. Setting the writers' stated intentions aside as one fallible piece of evidence (the intentional-fallacy debate), he weighs the medical model of disability (leveling and normalizing) against the social-constructivist model in which disability is a misfit between trait and environment. Because Sheldon has built a world — theoretical physics, accommodating friends, the comic book store — where his traits are advantages, even an 'alpha nerd' leader, they constitute an 'enability' rather than a disability, and the laughter is morally innocent.

samples.book: 140 - Avatar and Philosophy - Learning to See
samples.title: The Proud Disabled Person as Counterstory
samples.relation: Argues Toph Beifong is not a pejorative Supercrip stereotype but a Proud Disabled Person counterstory, using Hilde Lindemann's account of master narratives and identity: the BOD and IIH narratives (better-off-dead, irrationally happy) and the Supercrip all presume disability means suffering, while Toph's grumpiness, depth, and central role defy them. Her blindness is disability gain rather than tragedy, since being unsighted led her to learn earthbending from the original teachers, the badgermoles, and to immerse herself in seismic-sense bending full-time. Drawing on Elizabeth Barnes and Miranda Fricker's hermeneutical injustice, the chapter claims disability pride gives disabled viewers permission to celebrate themselves, and shows Toph driving the plot (inventing metalbending, training Aang in 'Bitter Work') instead of teaching non-disabled characters a moral lesson.

samples.book: 147 - Bioshock and Philosophy - Irrational Game, Rational Book
samples.title: Would You Kindly Evolve Today
samples.relation: Ledder reads Plasmids and ADAM as human enhancement technology and stages the real bioethics debate: therapy versus enhancement, transhumanist enthusiasm (whole-brain emulation like Eleanor's ADAM-collecting, Sandberg's morphological freedom) against fears of Splicer-like superhumans and eugenics. The Rapture arms race, where your Electric Bolt Plasmid goes obsolete and forces further splicing, dramatizes the coercive spiral of competitive enhancement, while Habermas's objection that genetically designing children turns them into projections grounds the reading of Jack, Fontaine's purchased and conditioned embryo triggered by 'would you kindly', as a metaphor for engineered autonomy destroyed. The chapter closes with disability critiques: maybe the problem is not the body but the social barriers that 'disable' it, so changing society might beat changing flesh.

samples.book: 153 - Disney and Philosophy - Truth, Trust, and a Little Bit of Pixie Dust
samples.title: What We Have Learned, or “Always Let Your Conscience Be Your Guide!”
samples.relation: Traces Disney disability from the medical model — Dopey as permanent childlike recipient of care, Gus-Gus, and LeFou, echoing Locke's claim that 'lunatics and idiots are never set free from the government of their parents' and Mill's restriction of liberty to those who can care for themselves — to the social model of disability in Finding Dory, where Charlie and Jenny's seashell trail makes the ocean an accommodating rather than disabling environment. Foucault's Birth of the Clinic explains how Gaston uses the asylum to control Maurice, medicine as power over lives. The chapter concludes that Pixar's Big Blue World embodies relational autonomy — Dory thriving 'in your own amazing Dory way' through supported interdependence — while nonverbal sidekicks Becky and Gerald show Dopey's disempowered comic-relief legacy survives.

samples.book: 095 - Downton Abbey and Philosophy - Thinking in That Manor
samples.title: 7. Disabled at Downton
samples.relation: Richmond weighs Downton's disability portrayals against disability-studies standards, citing Paul Longmore on media images and the 'super-crip' stereotype. Bates is the positive case: he endures Thomas's and O'Brien's ability-based discrimination, throws away the painful leg brace and rejects the idea that disability demands a medical cure, accepts disability as identity ('We all carry scars, Mr. Bates'), and marries Anna, refuting the era's stereotype that disabled people cannot be employees or lovers. Matthew is the harmful case: his paraplegia ends in Dr. Clarkson's 'spinal shock' misdiagnosis - a miracle cure - and talk of a 'normal life,' reinforcing the medical model and teaching real disabled viewers that their lives are over, so the author wants 'more Bateses, and fewer Matthews.'

samples.book: 084 - Leonard Cohen and Philosophy - Various Positions
samples.title: Leonard Cohen and Philosophy
samples.relation: Gary Shapiro treats The Future as a 'lyrical phenomenology' of time that stages multiple temporalities rather than one theory of time. 'The Future' evokes an apocalypse where the katechon - the Biblical restraining force holding back the end - no longer works, while 'Waiting for the Miracle' anatomizes passive deferral in a way Shapiro finds sharper than the Stoic critique of waiting by Seneca and Marcus Aurelius and Nietzsche's 'problem of those who wait,' opposing wasted chronos to the seized kairos of 'First We Take Manhattan.' 'Anthem's' crack that lets the light in gets a Gnostic reading, 'Democracy' is glossed through Derrida's 'democracy to come' as messianic, always-arriving futurity, and 'Closing Time' and 'Always' add honky-tonk eschatology and the vow of eternal love.

samples.book: 063 - Philip K. Dick and Philosophy - Do Androids Have Kindred Spirits
samples.title: Pink Light
samples.relation: This section argues that Dick's handling of the pink light enacts the Gnostic conviction that salvation comes from direct inner revelation rather than faith, sacraments, or church, cataloguing his competing theories: transmissions from a VALIS satellite that may itself be Yaldabaoth, mere ruler of the material realm, possession by Elijah, or his being Thomas the twin of Jesus. It weighs Dick's answers to why the true God permits the blind ruler (self-reflection, God's love of games, or our own labyrinth built to see if we could not escape) and the Gospel of Thomas's warning that the divine within will destroy us if we do not bring it forth.

samples.book: 082 - Jurassic Park and Philosophy - The Truth Is Terrifying
samples.title: Jurassic Park and Philosophy
samples.relation: Kenn Fisher reads the franchise as the extinction of the Great Chain of Being: from Plato's humans mid-way between gods and beasts, through Genesis dominion and Descartes's non-conscious animals, to Malcolm's 'God creates man. Man destroys God. Man creates dinosaurs' - with computers (Hammond's control room, Wikipedia, Google) replacing God at the top. He then tracks animals' ascent from property: Francione on welfare versus personhood, Bentham's 'Can they suffer?', and Singer's equality-as-prescription, applied to Dieter Stark tasering a compy (punished by the compys) versus the unexamined electric fences that keep InGen's 'zoo animals' caged. He closes with Carol Adams's meat-masculinity link - Roland Tembo will hunt only a male T. rex, the dinosaurs are all female - and holds up vegetarian Lex as hope that the Chain bends into a Circle.

samples.book: 074 - Planet of the Apes and Philosophy - Great Apes Think Alike
samples.title: Planet of the Apes and Philosophy
samples.relation: John Wilkins treats Caesar, who spares the neighbor he has beaten, as a Kantian exemplar whose reason lets him adopt the Categorical Imperative, contrasting him with the rational egoism of the film's human keepers and executives. He argues the film trades on the outdated Great Chain of Being, which Darwinian tree thinking dissolves: with no higher or lower species, only branching homologies, human nature must be continuous with ape nature, and talk of innate species essences must allow for statistical variation and dispositions rather than determination. Caesar's morality also needs more than reason, namely the primate dispositions of deference and empathy scaffolded by his human family, though Buck's instant moral conversion after enhancement shows the film is ambivalent about whether scaffolding alone explains it.

samples.book: 142 - The Avengers and Philosophy - Earth's Mightiest Thinkers
samples.title: Equal Opportunity—for Deities
samples.relation: Barkman argues the Marvel Universe's 'One-Above-All'—depicted as Stan Lee and Jack Kirby—is the eternal Judeo-Christian Creator, and arranges its beings in a graded hierarchy: the Living Tribunal as God's judge, cosmic beings like Eternity and Galactus, elders, sky fathers Odin and Zeus, down to mortals, with only God eternal and everything else, gods included, able to die yet enduring by His decree. Ontological rank guarantees nothing morally—Mephisto, the Goddess, and Hera are powerful and wicked, and even Hercules can be beaten by the Wrecking Crew. A free-will theodicy answers where evil came from: 'no other gods before me' never denied other gods' existence but commands loving the Good above all, which mortal Avengers like Thor, loving justice perfected by sacrificial love, manage as well as any deity.

samples.book: 127 - Blade Runner 2049 and Philosophy - This Breaks the World
samples.title: 20. Sympathy for the Existential Devils
samples.relation: James McLachlan reads the films through Sartre: replicants are made like penknives, with an essence before existence, and their drama is going 'off baseline' — the freedom of nothingness by which Batty murders his maker-gods (Tyrell the Father, Chew and Sebastian the trinity) and K disobeys everyone. Sartre's Satan from his Baudelaire biography, Blake's Orc and the Marriage of Heaven and Hell's contraries, and the Great Chain of Being's contradiction between filling one's place and moral freedom frame Luv as a perfect penknife, a 'good angel' who fulfills her vocation, while Batty and K are redeemed by the love that breaks their programming. 'More human than human' turns out to mean: existence precedes essence.

samples.book: 157 - Dungeons and Dragons and Philosophy - Read and Gain Advantage on All Wisdom Checks
samples.title: Dungeons and Dragons and Philosophy
samples.relation: Dadlez narrates an all-night RPG in which her disguised Romulan spy blew up the Enterprise and got herself shunned by her seminar colleagues, and asks whether role-playing evil makes the player morally complicit. Working through Hume's Standard of Taste claim that we cannot 'enter into' vicious sentiments and the puzzle of imagining morally deviant worlds, she argues the role-player is like an author or improvising actor: generating Waltonian fictional truths about a wicked character requires no first-person endorsement of the character's values, any more than method acting a villain requires sharing his ethics. The other players' real anger is explained not as imagined complicity but as resentment at having their collaborative Star Trek story hijacked into a triumph of the villain, and the 'Orc Holocaust' worry about XP-for-slaughter survives only as a caution that game-licensed 'shoot first' generalizations might bleed into real-world attitudes.

samples.book: 070 - Dungeons and Dragons and Philosophy - Raiding the Temple of Wisdom
samples.title: Dungeons and Dragons and Philosophy
samples.relation: Dadlez recounts playing an evil Romulan spy who befriended the Enterprise crew, blew up the ship, and got shunned by her real friends, and asks whether role-playing villains makes players complicit in immoral perspectives. Working from Hume on fiction that describes 'vicious manners' without disapprobation, and the imaginative-resistance debate (Walton, Gendler), she argues the role-player is like an author or improvisational actor who makes it fictional that a character holds wicked views without imaginatively endorsing them—no utilitarian or deontological truth of the game world endorsed her sabotage. Her friends' anger was really at her hijacking a collaborative story into one where the villain wins, and her only residual worry about the 'Orc Holocaust' of experience-point slaughter is that game generalizations about inherently hostile monsters might bleed into real-world prejudice about human groups.

samples.book: 170 - House and Philosophy - Everybody Lies
samples.title: Notes
samples.relation: Kajtar asks why viewers root for a double-murdering politician, framing the show through Tamar Gendler's puzzle of imaginative resistance: we would refuse to imagine Zoe's murder narrated as 'brave and noble,' yet House of Cards dissolves that resistance. Using Jenefer Robinson's claim that emotional engagement is necessary for understanding, the chapter shows how the Greenville first-pitch embarrassment, the Fort Sumter swim confession, and above all Frank's fourth-wall asides (telling us the real Gaffney eulogy, admitting 'I despise children') grant voyeuristic intimacy that humanizes him bite by bite - 'that's how you devour a whale.' By the time Frank frames Lucas Goodwin and Corrigan dies, we have adopted the morally deviant perspective, and the chapter warns this is exactly how politicians and artists seduce audiences into values we would otherwise reject.

samples.book: 171 - House of Cards and Philosophy - Underwood's Republic
samples.title: Notes
samples.relation: Takes up the puzzle of imaginative resistance (Gendler): while viewers would refuse to imagine that Frank's murder of Zoe was 'brave and noble', we end up rooting for his double murder and abuses of power. It explains this lack of resistance through the Greenville first-pitch confession, Frank's fourth-wall asides that grant us secret intimacy ('I despise children'), and Robinson's account of emotion-driven understanding-an engineered emotional seduction that doubles as a lesson in how politicians and artists manipulate audiences into morally deviant points of view.

samples.book: 175 - Iron Man and Philosophy - Facing the Stark Reality
samples.title: The Attack of the Chinese Room
samples.relation: Novy asks whether the Living Armor of 'The Mask in the Iron Man' — consciousness struck into it by lightning during the Whiplash fight, later tearing out its own heart to save Tony — really thinks. Turing's test and functionalism (any successful rescue of Yinsen is functionally equivalent, whatever the means) say only behavior matters, and Dennett's intentional stance has us treat the armor, like Darwin's burrow-plugging earthworms, as if it has beliefs and desires; against this, Leibniz's mill and Searle's Chinese Room — with Happy Hogan shuffling symbol cards he cannot read, held by 'Searle the Mandarin agent' — insist symbol manipulation never yields understanding. The chapter's reply: open the Mandarin's skull and you find only gray goop and neurons, so if behavior cannot ground understanding in the armor, it cannot in us either — we may all be in the Chinese Room.

samples.book: 074 - Planet of the Apes and Philosophy - Great Apes Think Alike
samples.title: Planet of the Apes and Philosophy
samples.relation: Don Fallis proposes deception rather than language as the personhood test: following Dennett, a deceiver must be a second-order intentional system who can want someone else to have a false belief, as when General Thade lies to Senator Sandar about Ari's kidnapping, Zira and Cornelius feign muteness before the Presidential Commission, and Caesar fakes his own electrocution in Conquest. The roles' reversal makes this a test for the films' mute humans too, while Descartes's beast machines, Wittgenstein on dogs that cannot simulate pain, and Lloyd Morgan's canon voice the skeptical reading of fake alarm calls and Koko's 'Cat did it.' Against them Fallis invokes Occam's Razor over Hare, Call and Tomasello's food-competition experiments: apes track who sees what, but they fail the misinformed false-belief version, so real apes may not be 'sneaky enough to be people.'

samples.book: 155 - Downton Abbey and Philosophy - The Truth Is Neither Here Nor There
samples.title: 11. What Mary Didn’t Know
samples.relation: Demeter argues that Mary's long hesitation over Matthew is radically underdetermined, sketching five rival interpretations of the same first-season events: emotional uncertainty, greed, fear of scandal over the Pamuk affair, bad conscience, and conflicting family pressure, each consistent with her behavior yet mutually exclusive. Via Frayn's play Copenhagen and the quantum measurement analogy he first treats this as a limit on human knowledge, then, using Dennett's 'Real Patterns' and Henry James's The Golden Bowl, defends the stronger metaphysical claim that there is no fact of the matter: psychological interpretation creates the very patterns it claims to find, so even Mary cannot know her own motives. What Mary didn't know may, on this view, be unknowable in principle.

samples.book: 095 - Downton Abbey and Philosophy - Thinking in That Manor
samples.title: 11. What Mary Didn’t Know
samples.relation: Demeter reconstructs five rival explanations of Mary's hesitation to accept Matthew - emotional uncertainty, greed, fear of social exclusion over Pamuk, bad conscience, and conflicting family pressures - and argues none can be singled out as true. Via Frayn's Copenhagen, Dennett's 'Real Patterns,' and Henry James's The Golden Bowl as read by Robert Pippin, he defends the indeterminacy of psychological interpretation: motives are accessed only through behavior filtered through the interpreter's own psychological apparatus, and on the stronger view there are no motivation-facts prior to interpretation at all. What Mary did not know about her own hesitation may therefore not be knowable in principle, by her or by us.

samples.book: 190 - The Ultimate Star Wars and Philosophy - You Must Unlearn What You Have Learned
samples.title: Notes
samples.relation: Uses a vintage Blue Snaggletooth action figure to illustrate Dennett's three stances - physical (AFA wear-grading of dented boots), design (why the Sears-exclusive mispack is valuable), and intentional (predicting whether Han would shoot first at a pedant correcting his parsec gaffe) - arguing that play trains a third-person science of mind that Descartes' first-person introspection and dualism could never verify. Dennett's account of religion as a misapplied intentional stance then explains begging the Falcon to 'hold together' and Zeus's lightning as projected intention, with the twist that children playing with figures know they are pretending while the superstitious mind does not.

samples.book: 063 - Philip K. Dick and Philosophy - Do Androids Have Kindred Spirits
samples.title: . . Because My Furnace Believed the House Was Cold
samples.relation: Explains Dennett's physical, design, and intentional stances through a disk drive 'reading' a disk and a thermostat we would never say 'believes' the room is cold, concluding that whether behavior counts as conscious is a choice of vocabulary, not a metaphysical difference. Dick's post-war world of convincing simulacra and economic necessity is the setting in which linguistic conventions shift, explaining Deckard's changed attitudes toward Luba Luft and Rachael.

samples.book: 160 - Fallout and Philosophy - Thinking Outside the Shelter
samples.title: Notes
samples.relation: Albert Spencer reads Fallout 4's synth crisis as a philosophy-of-mind allegory - Brotherhood dualism, Institute reductive physicalism, Railroad functionalism - which he grounds in the classical pragmatists: Peirce's sign-interpreting mind, James's stream of consciousness, and Dewey's interactive consciousness make personhood a matter of social participation rather than essence. Quests dramatize the stakes: 'Human Error' has Covenant's interrogation of Amelia Stockton enact Du Bois's double consciousness (self-understanding against a devaluing gaze, as with the tragic Phyllis Daily), the Sole Survivor of 'The Battle of Bunker Hill' and Far Harbor becomes Anzaldua's Nepantlera straddling the human/synth binary, and the Railroad's memory-wipe 'resets' reproduce the domination they fight by ignoring Crenshaw's intersectionality (the Feral Historian's case that the Railroad kills the selves it saves). Acadia, where DiMA murdered and replaced Captain Avery to preserve peace, becomes Jane Addams's test case of democracy as associated living - an imperfect, lying community that nonetheless offers the only future of shared synth-human personhood.

samples.book: 159 - The Expanse and Philosophy - So Far Out Into the Darkness
samples.title: Knuckles and the Augustín Gamarra
samples.relation: Deploys Crenshaw's intersectionality to explain why Naomi — the only Belter and only woman aboard the Rocinante — reads as a serial traitor: giving the protomolecule to Fred Johnson out of loyalty to the Belt, leaving Filip to escape Inaros's control of her through motherhood, and siding with Miller after the Dresden shooting ('as a Belter, Miller wasn't wrong'). It scales the analysis up to Belters as a collectively intersectional group — race, class, refugee status, and colonial occupation at once, as with the Weeping Somnambulist fired on carrying 55 refugees and the Ilus colonists framed through the European conquest of the Americas — then walks through Naomi's past with Marco (the Augustín Gamarra bombing that killed 516 people, her suicide attempt, 'the right to walk away') to show that resisting intersecting oppressions forces impossible, betrayal-laden choices, with her chosen family on the Roci as a model of solidarity that crosses identity lines.

samples.book: 073 - The Wire and Philosophy - This America, Man
samples.title: The Wire and Philosophy
samples.relation: Curry refuses to celebrate The Wire, arguing that Simon's class-based realism ('more about class than race') misrepresents Black urban life, and he contrasts it with Black film from New Jack City to Menace II Society where these issues were already explored. Reading scenes like Rawls's 'project nigger' murders no one cares about, Bunk shrugging at Stringer's unsolved killing, and McNulty telling Brianna that nobody will look into D'Angelo's death, he argues the show registers an indifference specific to Black life, not to the poor as such. Drawing on W.E.B. Du Bois's account of colonialism and the slave trade as the genesis of modern capital ('capital noir') and rejecting the intersectional race-class-gender frame as a 'discursive distraction', he demands a racial realism in Derrick Bell's sense: racism is permanent, the underclass is really an racialized undercaste, and the War on Drugs continues Jim Crow by other means.

samples.book: 088 - Justified and Philosophy - Shoot First, Think Later
samples.title: Justified and Philosophy
samples.relation: The chapter surveys Harlan's gendered violence - Ava's killing of Bowman, the routine roughing-up of Audrey's working girls, Robert Quarles's childhood prostitution - and uses Catharine MacKinnon's account of patriarchal power imbalance to explain victim-blaming, underreporting, and police disbelief of trauma responses in domestic-violence and rape cases. On prostitution it weighs sex-positive feminism against the objectification worry, concluding via Teri's line about 'sucking hillbilly dicks for money' that Audrey's women have little real choice even under Ava's management. Finally it brings in bell hooks's third-wave point that oppression cannot be split from race and class, plus Peggy McIntosh's invisible backpack of white privilege, to read Noble's Holler's isolation and the bombed black church as evidence that patriarchy in Justified is always also racial and economic.

samples.book: 149 - Black Panther and Philosophy - What Can Wakanda Offer the World_
samples.title: 11 Beastly Boys The Racial-Sexual Politics of Meat
samples.relation: Huerter reads M'Baku's 'I'm kidding. We are vegetarians' punchline through Carol Adams's sexual politics of meat and bell hooks's plantation patriarchy: since colonial meat-eating signified masculine mastery over nature (Plumwood's reason/nature dualism) while enslaved people were fed plant foods and cast as edible themselves, audiences primed by the racist cannibal trope expect M'Baku to be a savage, so his refusal of flesh turns the colonizer's gaze back on itself. Killmonger, by contrast, embodies the Black patriarchy produced by the American military-industrial complex ('He's one of ours'), a plantation patriarch whose hypermasculine conquest — killing Linda, burning the Herb garden, his defiant 'death was better than bondage' exit — replays colonial violence even in liberation's name, against which M'Baku's warrior-but-vegetarian politics marks a moral asymmetry.

samples.book: 185 - Saturday Night Live and Philosophy - Deep Thoughts Through the Decades
samples.title: Where in the Hell is Chris Rock
samples.relation: Wisnewski reads SNL's race comedy as applied philosophy of race: the Chase-Pryor 'Word Association' sketch shows Mr. Wilson's counter-slurs as an assertion of personhood against Mills's racial contract, Eddie Murphy's Mr. Robinson's Neighborhood and 'White Like Me' expose implicit bias and white privilege, and 'The Day Beyonce Turned Black' illustrates Du Bois's double consciousness. Appiah's racialism explains why Leslie Jones playing Trump strikes audiences as outrageous while white women play men routinely, and Appiah's biological anti-realism about race undercuts that reaction. 'Black Jeopardy' with Tom Hanks's MAGA-hatted Doug finds common ground across race that the 'Lives that Matter' ending sharply limits, Fanon's violence route is raised and set aside, and Crenshaw's intersectionality frames why cast diversity is more than skin-deep.

samples.book: 201 - Veronica Mars and Philosophy - Investigating the Mysteries of Life (Which Is a Bitch Until You Die)
samples.title: “A Pamphlet’s Not Going to Cover It”
samples.relation: Kasey Butcher and Megan Peters argue Veronica embodies a third-wave, sex-positive feminism: as jury foreman in 'One Angry Veronica' she refuses the 'Barbie' role the captain of industry assigns her; her over-the-top masquerades (flirting with store clerk Duane Anders, the temptation scenario at Patrick Nevin's door, mimicking Logan's manspreading) expose gender as a performance; and her defense of Carmen Ruiz against Tad's blackmail shows her grasp of how race, class, and gender intersect, per Kimberlé Crenshaw. Against the show's caricature of Lilith House as humorless 'feminist killjoys' picketing the Hearst rapes, they contend Veronica models a feminism that keeps femininity, sexuality, and play — refusing slut shaming while fighting for rape victims, an incest survivor, and blackmailed girls.

samples.book: 102 - Orphan Black and Philosophy - Grand Theft DNA
samples.title: 13. Sisterhood’s Back in Orphan Black
samples.relation: Recounts the rise and fall of second-wave sisterhood — the dream of a unified female voice that erased differences of race, class, sexuality, and nation until the 1980s backlash killed it — and argues Orphan Black resurrects a corrected version through Rosi Braidotti's posthumanism. The clones, disposable bodies of biogenetic capitalism, build a sisterhood that celebrates difference (grunge Sarah, dreads-and-lab-coat Cosima, suburban Alison, savage Helena) rather than enforcing sameness, and that welcomes the Others the Seventies excluded — gay Felix, Black Art, Hindu Raj — while white Western men like Paul remain the surveillance agents of the backlash. Through posthumanism's dissolution of fixed human identity, the chapter claims, feminism's old ideal returns both transformed and inclusive.

samples.book: 084 - Leonard Cohen and Philosophy - Various Positions
samples.title: Leonard Cohen and Philosophy
samples.relation: Bernard Wills takes the reference to The Cloud of Unknowing in 'The Window' as the key to Cohen's lifelong fascination with apophatic, negative mysticism - God sought beyond every image in a 'naked intent of love,' as in the medieval Cloud, Dionysius, Maimonides, and Kabbalah - against the kataphatic way of affirmation. He reads Recent Songs as an album of exile and the play of union and separation ('Un Canadien Errant,' 'Ballad of the Absent Mare'), where the incarnate Word is 'stuttered' and 'frozen,' a passion without resurrection. Cohen's later Zen turn is thus prefigured: the emptiness of sunyata and the Neo-Platonic descent from and return to the One are positive nothingness - self-overcoming in the service of compassion rather than the black-romantic nihilism of self-annihilation.

samples.book: 141 - Avatar_ The Last Airbender and Philosophy - Wisdom from Aang to Zuko
samples.title: Avatar The Reunion of Multiplicity
samples.relation: Strok explains the swamp visions in 'The Swamp' through Plotinus and Augustine: Katara's dead mother, Sokka's Yue, and Aang's unknown giggling girl are, respectively, memory, attention, and expectation, Augustine's three presents, while Plotinus's hierarchy of One, Intellect, and world Soul, with time as 'the life of the Soul,' lets what is successive for us be simultaneous from eternity. Huu's banyan-grove tree, one organism spread over miles, is read as Neoplatonic emanation, and Toph's later root-connectedness in LoK shows the ability is not exclusive to the Avatar. Since past and future Avatar selves are thus present to Aang, death, like time, is an illusion, which underwrites his refusal to kill Ozai.

samples.book: 126 - Stranger Things and Philosophy - Thus Spake the Demogorgon
samples.title: 7. The Mind Flayer through a Gnostic Lens
samples.relation: Ewing reads the Mind Flayer as the Demiurge of the Upside Down, a dark derivative copy of our world complete with replicated Castle Byers and school decorations: he surveys Plato's Timaeus craftsman who shapes chaotic matter on the model of the Forms, Plotinus's One and its secondary demiurge, and the Gnostic variants, from the Valentinian just-but-imperfect craftsman to the Sethian Yaldabaoth, a serpent-faced false god who steals divine power. Because the Mind Flayer hive-minds Will and the demodogs, wants to conquer our dimension as a 'master race,' and hates the real world rather than serving it, the chapter concludes it matches the Sethian evil Demiurge, an incorporeal entity playing at being god.

samples.book: 090 - Dracula and Philosophy - Dying to Know
samples.title: Dracula and Philosophy
samples.relation: Willis and Strunk read the scene where Dracula forces Mina to drink blood from his bare chest through Plotinus's Enneads: the mutual blood exchange is a dark unicity, a perverted oneness joining life and death, through which the soulless, blood-dependent Count tries to steal Mina's agency, Intellect, and her link to the world soul because he cannot be self-sufficient or create his own meaning. Their interconnected minds are also his undoing - Mina's hypnotic bond tracks Dracula to his coffin, and his destruction at Van Helsing's hands frees her - so the chapter concludes that this perversion of Plotinian oneness exposes our fear that the veil between the living and the dead is dangerously thin.

samples.book: 140 - Avatar and Philosophy - Learning to See
samples.title: Avatar The Reunion of Multiplicity
samples.relation: Strok explains the swamp visions in 'The Swamp' (Katara's dead mother, Sokka's Yue, Aang's glimpse of the girl who will be Toph) through Plotinus's teaching that time is 'the life of the Soul' and Augustine's three presents of memory, attention, and expectation, so that past and future are present to the soul and Huu's 'time is an illusion and so is death' becomes literal metaphysics. The banyan-grove tree, one organism spread over miles, models Neoplatonic emanation from the One, and this unity explains the Avatar's communion with past and future selves as well as Aang's refusal to kill Ozai, since death, like time, is a misperception.

samples.book: 113 - Jimi Hendrix and Philosophy - Experience Required
samples.title: 17. The Cry of Love
samples.relation: Reads Hendrix as a romantic idealist on a Platonic-Neoplatonic arc: 'Room Full of Mirrors' shatters the cave wall and its projections toward The One, whose presence is pursued through eros with the veiled Beloved of Plotinus — the semi-divine feminine of 'Little Wing,' 'One Rainy Wish,' and 'Angel.' Hegel's Zeitgeist and world-spirit then frame the planned First Rays of the New Rising Sun as music meant to carry humanity's collective evolution, with Hendrix as Hegel's 'spiritual workman' and self-described messenger ('I am only a messenger and you are a Sheep in the process of evolution').

samples.book: 063 - Philip K. Dick and Philosophy - Do Androids Have Kindred Spirits
samples.title: Remembrance of Being, Passed
samples.relation: Reads Ubik's anti-chronological regressions — rocket to jet to biplane, 1992 decaying into 1939 — through Dick's 'orthogonal time' peeling onion-like layers toward greater Being, which Dick himself compared to Plotinus's concentric emanations from the One beyond all language and comprehension. Dick's 1974 pink-light experience is interpreted as Platonic anamnesis, recovered memory of the forms in a parallel time-stream, shading into the Gnostic conviction that our flawed material universe was created by an imperfect god.

samples.book: 172 - The Hunger Games and Philosophy - A Critique of Pure Treason
samples.title: The Hunger Games and Philosophy
samples.relation: Jason Eberl treats the muttations, jabberjays that mimic speech without understanding, tracker jackers, the wolf-mutts with Glimmer's eyes that torment Cato, and the lizard-mutts hissing Katniss's name, alongside real chimeras (geeps, the SCID-hu mouse, Balaban's quail-chick brain transplants, Weissman's human-neural mouse) to ask whether biotechnology could create a person. Working through Boethius's definition of a person as an 'individual substance of a rational nature' and Locke's 'thinking intelligent Being' that can consider itself the same over time, he argues that human DNA alone confers no personhood, while a chimera genuinely capable of self-conscious rational thought would be a person whose weaponized creation and lab captivity would violate its rights, which is why ethicists allow mouse chimeras but hesitate with primates. He notes that the Gamemakers' refusal to see tributes as persons is exactly the move that made slavery and Nazi dehumanization possible, and that Katniss's suspicion about whether the mutts remember their deaths is the right ethical question to keep open.

samples.book: 163 - Game of Thrones and Philosophy - Logic Cuts Deeper Than Swords
samples.title: Game of Thrones and Philosophy
samples.relation: Matthew Tedesco reads Bran's coma and Drogo's living death as biomedical ethics: Jaime's 'good clean death' for Bran raises active versus passive euthanasia, and with James Rachels he argues the AMA's killing/letting-die distinction merely licenses more suffering, while Brock recasts withdrawal of treatment as intentional killing anyway. The Bran case frames end-of-life decisions for children - the Johns Hopkins and Baby John Pearson cases - and whether parents may weigh a handicap's burden on the family, a question made vivid by Bran riding Hodor. Dany's smothering of Drogo, by contrast, does not strike readers as murder because personhood rather than biological humanity carries moral standing: on Tooley's self-consciousness, Warren's five criteria, or Marquis's future-like-ours, Drogo is human but no longer a person - which leads straight to Peter Singer's claim that killing a disabled infant who is not a person may not be wrong at all, leaving us to ask whether our recoil is reason or taboo.

samples.book: 068 - The Walking Dead and Philosophy - Zombie Apocalypse Now
samples.title: The Walking Dead and Philosophy
samples.relation: Allaire argues walkers have no moral value and can be killed without remorse: a Bentham-style act-utilitarian tally favors killing any walker, and, following Kant, genetic humanity is neither necessary nor sufficient for membership in the moral community. Applying Mary Anne Warren's five personhood criteria, he shows walkers lack pain response (Hannah's severed half still dragging itself at Rick), language, planning (Glenn's gun-bag mission versus aimless shuffling), and self-reflection, so as beings incapable of duty they can have no rights. Morgan's inability to shoot his walker-wife and Rick's 'I'm sorry this happened to you' illustrate Kant's 'duality of the human situation' — we irrationally project personhood onto former people — and our hesitation is precisely the walkers' greatest advantage.

samples.book: 089 - Steve Jobs and Philosophy - For Those Who Think Different
samples.title: Steve Jobs and Philosophy
samples.relation: Munkittrick argues that because personhood cannot be defined (trait lists like 'long-term planning' are circular) and behavior cannot prove an inner mind—as Searle's Chinese Room thought experiment shows—people have always identified persons intuitively, and Pixar trained Millennials to do exactly that. He reads the Pixar canon in three stages: Toy Story's self-aware Buzz as nascent non-human personhood, the Human-as-Partner films (Ratatouille's Remy and Linguini, WALL-E and EVE, Monsters, Inc.'s Sully and Boo, Up's Carl and Dug) as mutual recognition of persons across species lines, and The Incredibles as showing that even enhanced 'super-humans' face otherization—so a generation primed by these films will accept AI, animals, and uplifted beings as bearers of rights.

samples.book: 202 - The Walking Dead and Philosophy - Shotgun. Machete. Reason
samples.title: The Walking Dead and Philosophy
samples.relation: Si Sheppard reads the comic through Realist state-formation theory: Shane's leadership rests on borrowed prestige and dies with him, West Central Prison collapses into anarchy because Rick never establishes a monopoly on legitimate force—letting Tyreese's vigilante murder pass—nor any institution beyond his personal authority, while the Governor's Woodbury thrives on fear, arenas, and bread-and-circuses. Citing Machiavelli's prince who is feared rather than loved, Weber's definition of the state, and Bismarck's unifying wars, he argues the prison loses the 'second anarchy' rivalry with Woodbury for want of scouting, sabotage, coalition-building, or any command structure that survives Rick's absences. Rick's confession that he would kill everyone in the Alexandria Safe Zone to keep Lori safe is post-moral Realism, yet he was 'a bad founding father' who only finally learns to build an army instead of relying on himself.

samples.book: 068 - The Walking Dead and Philosophy - Zombie Apocalypse Now
samples.title: The Walking Dead and Philosophy
samples.relation: Si Sheppard grades The Walking Dead's three settlements by political Realism: the Governor's Woodbury - cohesive, feared rather than loved, feeding his people arena spectacle to keep them from turning on him - beats Rick's West Central Prison, which never becomes a state at all. Rick lets Tyreese's vigilante murder pass, ruling as a first-among-equals with no institutions, no constitution, and no monopoly of legitimate force in Weber's sense, then covertly guns down Thomas and Dexter while hiding behind his cop credibility - 'it's me or you' reasoning indistinguishable from Shane's. Realism cares about power, not morality, so Rick's flaw is not cruelty but the absence of institution-building: he was never a bad father, just a bad founding father, who only becomes a Realist after Alexandria falls.

samples.book: 138 - Alien and Philosophy - I Infest Therefore I Am
samples.title: Easing Back on the APC’s Throttle
samples.relation: Treats Engineers, Xenomorphs, and humans as states and reads the APC debate through Thucydides' Melian dialogue ('the strong do what they will') and the jus in bello criteria of discrimination, military necessity, and proportionality. It concludes that Ripley's 'nuke the site from orbit' and Vasquez's nerve gas are vengeance masquerading as realism - the Xeno threat is no longer imminent, so Walzer's 'supreme emergency' is unavailable - while Hudson's withdrawal (even Burke's species-preservation plea) fits both realism and just war restraint; the Ben Tre 'we destroyed the town to save it' fiasco in Vietnam is the cautionary parallel.

samples.book: 061 - Sherlock Holmes and Philosophy - The Footprints of a Gigantic Mind
samples.title: The Seven Percent Conclusion
samples.relation: Malloy names boredom, not Moriarty, as Holmes's true nemesis, sorting his moods through Heidegger's three types: boredom by something (the mind-reading demonstration in 'The Cardboard Box' that bores Holmes but astounds Watson), boredom with everything ('The Noble Bachelor's' 'unwelcome social summonses'), and profound boredom — the 'black moods' behind the seven-per-cent solution, which Heidegger says reveals beings as a whole in remarkable indifference. Against Schopenhauer's pendulum swinging between pain and boredom, and Nietzsche's 'against boredom even gods struggle in vain,' Pascal's and Kierkegaard's verdict that boredom is the root of all evil explains Jeremy Paul's suggestion that Holmes invented Moriarty as an equal opponent to keep the game alive. Religion, Pascal's and Kierkegaard's cure, cannot save the modern Holmes, so work, amusement, and drugs merely treat symptoms of modernity itself.

samples.book: 119 - Twin Peaks and Philosophy - That's Damn Fine Philosophy!
samples.title: 17. Through Plastic Our Secrets Seen
samples.relation: Uses Schopenhauer's World as Will to explain why the citizens of Twin Peaks keep living lives they despise: all willing arises from deficiency and suffering, so Shelly cannot leave Leo, Ben cannot face his children, and Ed is consumed oscillating between Norma and Nadine, while the blind will — not reflection — determines who we become. Since only pain is known directly and its absence slides into boredom and banality (Ed's restless drama-making), the town's double lives — Jacoby's coconut tapes hiding Laura's confession, Bobby's dealing, Ben's brothel — are the will's concealed kernels. Laura's wrapped corpse then functions as the reveal: death shows each character's truth, and the chapter closes by turning Socrates' unexamined life against itself, asking what happens when self-examination only uncovers what we wished hidden, as Cooper's daily-present advice offers the lone consolation.

samples.book: 199 - True Detective and Philosophy - A Deeper Kind of Darkness
samples.title: Notes
samples.relation: Reconstructs Rust's scattered remarks — the world as 'one giant gutter,' procreation as the hubris of yanking a soul out of nonexistence into the thresher — into an explicit anti-natalist argument, testing each premise and conceding procreation is selfish while questioning whether every life nets more harm than good. It presents David Benatar's asymmetry between the absence of pain (always good) and the absence of pleasure (bad only for someone deprived), illustrating it with the show: contraception as procreative duty, the wrongness of conceiving in Tuttle's Louisiana, and the emptiness of Childress' temple as a good in itself. The chapter concludes that Rust's 'opt out of a raw deal' is philosophically defensible, with Schopenhauer's desire-pendulum and Hobbes' 'nasty, brutish, and short' backing the claim that most lives are bad.

samples.book: 262 - Dr. Seuss and Philosophy - Oh, the Thinks You Can Think!
samples.title: My Troubles Are Going to Have Troubles with Me Schopenhauer, Pessimism, and Nietzsche
samples.relation: Jacob Held pits Schopenhauer's pessimism against Nietzschean affirmation using I Had Trouble in Getting to Solla Sollew. He reads Schopenhauer's will-to-life and 'pendulum between pain and boredom' into Seuss's endlessly striving characters, and treats the mirage-towns Solla Sollew and Boola Boo Ball as proof there is no escape from suffering. The protagonist's final line, 'I've bought a big bat... now my troubles are going to have troubles with me,' becomes Nietzsche's yes-saying: instead of the ascetic renunciation Schopenhauer prescribes, Seuss's child-hero affirms life, redeeming its accidents the way Nietzsche's eternal-recurrence thought experiment and 'become a child' passage in Zarathustra demand.

samples.book: 173 - Inception and Philosophy - Because It's Never Just a Dream
samples.title: An Old Man, Filled with Regret . .
samples.relation: Matthew Brophy argues the film's plot makes most sense if it is an addicted gamer's MMORPG session: Cobb is an avatar, his corporate pursuers are named COBOL after the old programming language, dream 'architects' mirror world-designers like Second Life's Furia Freeloader with her Escher Relativity House, and Mal is a 'gamer's widow' whose in-game suicide deleted her character so she could return to the real family Cobb abandoned. Using the 'egocentric predicament' that no one can access another's mind, he suggests shared dreaming can only really happen on servers, and via Borges's map that covered the empire and Baudrillard's claim that the simulacrum outlives the real he reads Second Life replicas (the virtual Texas A&M campus) as the preferred level of reality decaying the actual one. He then deploys Bostrom's simulation argument — we may already be conscious simulations — and casts Yusuf's basement dreamers, Xiao Yi's Warcraft suicide, and WoW-neglect cases as modern Lotus-Eaters, concluding that the ending is a 'long con': the real inception planted in Cobb the belief that his game is real, so he will one day wake 'an old man, filled with regret, waiting to die alone.'

samples.book: 061 - Sherlock Holmes and Philosophy - The Footprints of a Gigantic Mind
samples.title: The Evil Genius that Turns Moriarty into a Brain in a Vat
samples.relation: Samardzija reads Star Trek's holodeck Moriarty as Descartes updated: Data plays Holmes on the holodeck while Dr. Pulaski's Nietzschean jibe (from 'The Illogical Necessary' in Human, All Too Human) denies that computation can be human, and the holographic Moriarty proves his sentience not by deduction but by feelingCrowded intuitions first and then invoking Descartes' cogito ergo sum to Picard. In 'Ship in a Bottle' he nests a simulation of the Enterprise inside the Holmes holodeck to trick the crew into believing he has escaped — an evil-genius, brain-in-a-vat scenario that ends with Picard admitting our own reality 'might be nothing more than an elaborate simulation.' The paradox is that only the unemotional android Data can detect the deception, so rationality bars him from humanity while Moriarty stays eternally deceived into thinking he has become human — and Doyle's own 'hereditary tendencies' account of Moriarty's evil, the chapter notes, is a Victorian biological determinism the hologram rebels against.

samples.book: 094 - Divergent and Philosophy - The Factions of Life
samples.title: 11. Should We Execute the Erudite
samples.relation: Michaud and Watkins ask whether Roth is right that the knowledge-hoarding Erudite are so dangerous we might need to eliminate them, and answer that knowledge is dangerous in three ways. Following Foucault ('it is impossible for knowledge not to engender power'), the powerful define what counts as knowledge - from the church blessing feudalism to the medical community pathologizing gay and transgender people - and following Piaget, new knowledge threatens the interconnected belief schemas (diagrammed as beliefs resting on beliefs) that keep 'faction before blood' and our sense of being special stable, which is why Divergents, evolution, and Copernicus provoke such violent disequilibrium. A Descartes-style simulation scenario - you may be inside Roth's world right now, weeded out for reading the books - and David Lewis's point that investigating knowledge destroys it then show that the real danger is not knowledge but the arrogance of certainty: Jeanine was never a true Erudite.

samples.book: 189 - The Ultimate Star Trek and Philosophy - The Search for Socrates
samples.title: Notes
samples.relation: Uses the holodeck as a working model for the ancient claim that everyday reality is appearance: Plato's cave shadows, maya in Hindu and Buddhist thought, and Bostrom's simulation argument (his ancestor simulations mirrored in Data and Geordi's endless Holmes holoprograms) converge with quantum "holographic universe" speculation to suggest our universe may be a cosmic holoprogram with limit conditions like light speed as processing boundaries. Moriarty seizing the Enterprise in "Ship in a Bottle", Vic Fontaine, and the EMH dramatize self-aware programs confronting their code, and the chapter argues our "free will" may be similarly bounded - Data-as-Holmes must stay in character, and Picard "can't transcend the script" any more than his NPCs can. Picard's closing admission that our reality may be "an elaborate simulation running inside a little device" delivers the skeptical upshot, alongside the ethical question of whether self-aware holograms deserve rights.

samples.book: 062 - Inception and Philosophy - Ideas to Die For
samples.title: An Old Man, Filled with Regret . .
samples.relation: Brophy argues Cobb's shared dreams are best modeled on MMORPG virtual worlds like Second Life and World of Warcraft: Ariadne is a world-building architect in the mold of Second Life's Escher Relativity House, dreamers are avatars, and the film's looping architectures mirror the toroidal grids of game worlds. Reading the film as an addict's 'long con', he claims the real inception was planting in Cobb's own head the idea that his game-world is real: Mal is a 'gamer's widow' whose in-game suicide deleted her character, and Cobb is the avatar of an unseen addicted player who has forgotten the game. Borges's map that covers the empire, Baudrillard's claim that the simulacrum becomes the preferred reality, Bostrom's simulation argument, and Homer's lotus-eaters all support the warning that we already prefer simulated worlds, so the last shot means the real Cobb will one day wake as an old man filled with regret.

samples.book: 241 - The Philosophy of Documentary Film
samples.title: 32_LaRocca_Chapter_031.html
samples.relation: LaRocca argues that Casey Affleck's I'm Still Here, in which Joaquin Phoenix faked a drug-addled retirement and hip-hop career, is best understood as a 'hoax-verite' whose collapse of the boundary between real and represented turns it into a Baudrillardian simulacrum and hyperreal artifact, a documentary of images 'without an original referent.' Against Noel Carroll's account of documentary as a film of presumptive assertion and Plantinga's assertive stance, LaRocca shows how Affleck exploited audience faith (staged home movies, the David Letterman 'beat down') so that the film's metaphysical, epistemic and ethical status transformed once the fraud was confirmed. He invokes Hegel's remarks on abstract individuality and compares the case to Herzog's 'ecstatic truth,' Roth's and Kaufman's metafiction, to argue the deception paradoxically discloses deeper truths about what documentary is.

samples.book: 308 - The Palgrave Handbook of Popular Culture as Philosophy
samples.title: 21. Black Mirror as Philosophy A Dark Reflection of Human Nature
samples.relation: The chapter asks whether Black Mirror condemns technology or human nature, and argues for the latter: the 'black mirror' reflects the viewer's character. It tests and rejects the reading of the show as depicting Bostrom-style existential risk or superintelligence (via 'Metalhead' and 'San Junipero') and rejects that Clark and Chalmers's extended-mind coupling (the 'grain' in 'The Entire History of You,' 'Arkangel,' 'Crocodile') destroys human identity. Drawing on Frankfurt School critique—Adorno and Horkheimer's culture industry, Marcuse's one-dimensional man—and Plato's and Aristotle's natural-versus-artificial distinction, it concludes technology is an agency-less imitation that magnifies preexisting human vices, and closes with Benjamin's reproducibility thesis and Bandersnatch's interactivity to suggest the show can prompt viewers to confront their own darkness.

samples.book: 122 - Westworld and Philosophy - Mind Equals Blown
samples.title: “Do you even know where you are ”
samples.relation: Arvan argues the entire series, lab included, literally takes place inside a videogame, citing physically impossible events (Teddy's bullets cannot hurt the Man in Black, William steps onto a moving train, workers appear instantly in a single unbroken shot) and NPC-like loops of the lab staff. He then claims Descartes had it backwards: whether we are in a dream, Spinoza's God's mind, or a simulation (Bostrom's hypothesis, extended by his own peer-to-peer variant that would explain quantum indeterminacy and relativity), to be simulated is still to be real. Via Chalmers-style structuralism, anything structured and functioning like a person is a person, so hosts who walk, talk, love, and suffer are persons — and the humans' rape, torture, and murder of them, like our treatment of Siri and Watson, is dehumanization on a par with slavery and the Holocaust.

samples.book: 196 - Terminator and Philosophy - I'll Be Back, Therefore I Am
samples.title: NOTES
samples.relation: Dunn reads Descartes' bete-machine doctrine (animals as soulless automata explicable by 'billiard ball' mechanics) against the Terminator universe, since Descartes' two tests for true men - genuine language and versatile reason - are in fact passed by the machines: the T-101 deploys 'Hasta la vista, baby' hours after learning not to sound like a dork and marshals skills far beyond a clock. Sarah Connor instead locates the soul in the heart, and via Spinoza's conatus - the instinctual valuation of one's own existence that Terminators lack ('no emotion about it one way or another') - she judges even linguistically brilliant machines soulless and irrational, as Mary Midgley says of computers that do not know what matters. Kyle's line about 'dreaming about dogs' closes the chapter: by the Sarah Connor criterion dogs are ensouled sentinels, the very thing Descartes denied.

samples.book: 191 - Star Wars and Philosophy Strikes Back - This Is the Way
samples.title: “An Energy Field Created by All Living Things”
samples.relation: Baur argues that the Jedi metaphysics is non-dualistic rather than a simple good-versus-evil opposition, reading the Force through Spinoza: ideas become more or less true as they cohere with other ideas (so 'Luke loves Leia', 'Han is a mercenary', and 'Vader is evil' all need qualification), and everything seeks power by the conatus that Yoda and Obi-Wan attribute to the Force. The light side seeks power in balance with other things while the dark side, per the Sith Rule of Two, plays a zero-sum game. Luke's arc mirrors Oedipus: denying his inherited psychological likeness to Vader only enacts it, and only by acknowledging and owning the anger he inherited from his father can he gain power over it and enable Vader's redemption and his own.

samples.book: 061 - Sherlock Holmes and Philosophy - The Footprints of a Gigantic Mind
samples.title: The House that Holmes Built
samples.relation: Kate Rufa reads Holmes as Spinoza's 'just man': Watson's 'calculating machine' verdict in The Sign of the Four, his unshaken calm while baiting Moriarty before the Reichenbach leap in 'The Final Problem', and the geometric 'Book of Life' of A Study in Scarlet all show passion mastered by reason into adequate ideas and true freedom. The twist is the cocaine: shooting up between cases means Holmes sacrifices his conatus (the striving to persist in being) to keep his mind at a godlike pitch of activity, a God-complex no finite mode can sustain. Moriarty, equally rational but ruled by passive affects, is the shadow of this ideal, echoing Socrates' Apology point that harming others inevitably harms oneself.

samples.book: 063 - Philip K. Dick and Philosophy - Do Androids Have Kindred Spirits
samples.title: The Origin and Nature of Affective Disorder
samples.relation: Using the opening of VALIS, the section explains Gloria's suicide through Spinoza's account of the passions: imagining we are hated without cause breeds hatred, and Spinoza's lone remark on suicide says those who kill themselves are 'impotent in mind,' overcome by external causes opposed to their nature, since our essence just is the conatus, the striving to persist in being. It then itemizes Fat's three tragedies (Gloria's death, the divorce, losing his son) as accumulating external causes that overwhelmed him into his own suicide attempt, and presents his therapist Maurice's 'take responsibility for your own life' as implicitly Spinozan advice.

samples.book: 300 - Who Is Who_ The Philosophy of Doctor Who
samples.title: Who is Who
samples.relation: Focused on the 'Monstrous Other' and the 'base under siege' story, the chapter uses Hegel's master-slave struggle for recognition and Sartre's 'the look' to read Cybermen, the Flood ('Waters of Mars') and the Silurians as Others through which humans define themselves, with Levinas on the face and history. Its final section frames the Doctor and the Master as Gothic doubles of love and strife, using Spinoza's monism, principle of sufficient reason and conatus to argue the power-hungry Master paradoxically fits Spinoza's system better than the order-imposing 'Dark Doctor.'

samples.book: 173 - Inception and Philosophy - Because It's Never Just a Dream
samples.title: Group Will
samples.relation: Testerman argues the film's heist is ironic because nobody in it acts from conscious will: citing Libet's readiness-potential experiments and Penfield's stimulation cases, she claims the feeling of willing is a post-hoc 'epistemic illusion,' so Fischer's inception merely dramatizes what happens all the time — Cobb's 'all experience is inception' becomes a thesis about ordinary agency, with Spinoza's dictum that freedom is ignorance of the causes of our actions as its motto. She reads the plot through this lens: Saito's unexamined hunger for power silently drives the team's 'group will,' Cobb's 'positive emotion trumps negative emotion' tactic exploits the limbic system, and cheaper tricks (Arthur's elephant, foot-in-the-door, subliminal advertising) would have worked as well. Against Socrates she concludes the unexamined life is perfectly livable, since introspection can never reach the subconscious causes of behavior.

samples.book: 160 - Fallout and Philosophy - Thinking Outside the Shelter
samples.title: Notes
samples.relation: The chapter argues modding is the deepest freedom Bethesda-era Fallout offers: Sartre and Beauvoir's absolute freedom and facticity explain why vanilla players merely pick among given priorities while modders inject new meaning into the game, constrained but not determined by the Creation Engine. Spinoza's causal determinism becomes a model of 'immanent freedom' — just as Spinoza's agent is free by understanding their place in Nature's web of causes, the modder is free by grasping how they fit into the load orders, plugin files, and tools of the Creation Kit. Simone Weil's ideal of self-directed labor culminates the argument: Fallout: London's five-year, unpaid total conversion (the Atta-Boy, Churchill the bulldog, the punk-anarchist Pistols) embodies the convergence of thought and action that Moira Brown's line about putting broken glass back together captures.

samples.book: 184 - The Office and Philosophy - Scenes from the Unexamined Life
samples.title: The Office and Philosophy
samples.relation: Lonergan and Wisnewski read 'Grief Counseling' and 'Safety Training' as a case study in death-denial: Michael cannot parse the euphemism 'we lost Ed Truck,' Kelly must teach him to be sad, and Creed's report of the decapitation forces the Heideggerian realization that death is his own not-to-be-outstripped possibility, not just a fact of life. The office deflects with movie plots and euphemism (Jim's 'seriously hurt' about the rooftop stunt), Pam's eulogy for Toby's bird shows how mourning ritual copes with mortality, and Michael's longing to be remembered - hospital wings named after him, saving his own life - exemplifies Kierkegaard's 'world-historical' life as an ego defense, with living subjectively the recommended but unexplained alternative. Becker's thesis that all culture is a fabricated protest against death frames the whole chapter.

samples.book: 243 - The Philosophy of Christopher Nolan
samples.title: Spinning Tops and Brains in Vats

samples.title: The End

Chan contrasts Zhuangzi's butterfly dream with Inception's plot: Zhuangzi forgets his self, dreams without planning, and ends in the 'transformation and unity' of dreamer and butterfly, whereas Cobb's self is constantly highlighted — he plans missions, codes his dreams with motifs (the spinning top, the dream machine, the faceless children, distinct locations, weather, crosscutting), and can never fuse dream and reality. He then goes east - Zhuangzi's butterfly, Indra's net of mutually reflecting jewels, Schopenhauer's universe dreamed by a single dreamer, William James's many consciousnesses - to ask how many times we must die before waking, ending with Buddhism: 'Buddha means awakened one', and Cobb's turning from the top enacts Nirvana, where the real-versus-dream question stops pertaining.

samples.book: 142 - The Avengers and Philosophy - Earth's Mightiest Thinkers

samples.book: 086 - Girls and Philosophy - This Book Isn't a Metaphor for Anything
samples.title: Girls and Philosophy

samples.book: 066 - Neil Gaiman and Philosophy - Gods Gone Wild!

samples.book: 199 - True Detective and Philosophy - A Deeper Kind of Darkness
